Why Sustainable Data Acquisition?
A smart farm with 500 IoT sensors sampling every second generates 43.2 million readings per day — roughly 788 GB per year. Yet soil moisture changes only every 15–20 minutes. Nearly 95% of that data is redundant.

Adaptive Sampling
Fixed-interval sampling wastes energy by repeatedly recording identical values. Adaptive sampling varies the collection interval proportionally to the rate of change in the sensor reading: the faster the value shifts, the higher the sampling frequency.

Duty Cycling: Sleep to Save
The wireless radio consumes up to 60% of a sensor node's total energy. Duty cycling addresses this by alternating the node between ACTIVE and SLEEP states rather than keeping the radio on continuously.
Average Power Formula
At a 5% duty cycle: Pactive = 50 mW, Psleep = 0.1 mW → Pavg ≈ 2.6 mW — a ~95% reduction.
Energy Distribution
Real-world result: Smart Parking Sensors wake every 30 seconds, check for a vehicle, then sleep — achieving a 5-year battery life.

Wake-Up Radio: Eliminating Idle Listening
In traditional IoT nodes, the main radio remains on waiting for a message — the dominant source of wasted energy. A Wake-Up Radio replaces constant listening with an ultra-low-power receiver that activates the main radio only when a valid signal arrives.

Sensor Selection, Scheduling & Event-Triggered Sensing
Intelligent Sensor Selection
When 20 nearby temperature sensors differ by only ±0.2°C, activating all of them is wasteful. AI-driven scheduling uses clustering and information gain to activate only the most informative subset.
K-Means Clustering
Information Gain
Reinforcement Learning
Result: 100 sensors → 25 active sensors — 75% reduction in communication cost.
Event-Triggered Sensing
Rather than sampling every second, transmit only when a reading crosses a meaningful threshold. An air quality node monitoring PM2.5 can drop from 86,400 readings/day to ~5,000 — a 94% reduction — without missing a single pollution event.

Do not transmit; retry later

In-Sensor Processing: Edge AI with TinyML
Transmitting raw sensor data to the cloud is energy-intensive. Edge AI deploys a lightweight machine-learning model directly on the sensor node, so only the result of inference travels over the network — not the raw payload.
Traditional Camera Pipeline
Raw video frame: 2 MB → transmitted to cloud → AI inference performed remotely. High bandwidth, high energy cost.
Edge AI Pipeline
TinyML model runs on-device → transmits only: "Person detected, confidence 98%" → 30 Bytes. A 99% reduction in transmitted data.
TinyML Frameworks
TensorFlow Lite, Edge Impulse, and TinyML enable model deployment on microcontrollers with as little as 256 KB of RAM.

Sensor Fusion & Data Compression
Sensor Fusion
A single sensor can fail or produce unreliable readings. Fusing outputs from Camera + Radar + GPS + LiDAR through a unified decision engine yields higher confidence and fault tolerance. An autonomous vehicle example: Camera says "pedestrian", Radar says "object" → Fusion engine concludes Pedestrian detected at 98% accuracy.
Kalman Filter
Bayesian Network
Deep Learning Fusion
Data Compression
Wireless transmission costs 1,000× more energy than a CPU instruction. Compressing before transmitting is therefore critical to sustainable pipelines.
Lossless
Huffman, LZW, Run-Length — full fidelity recovery
Lossy
JPEG, MPEG, Wavelet — acceptable precision trade-off
Typical result: 100 MB → 25 MB at a 4:1 compression ratio, before a single byte travels wirelessly.

Data Quality, Missing Values & Bias Detection
Low-quality data feeds poor AI models, leading to wrong decisions at scale. Quality must be enforced across five dimensions, and gaps or skews must be corrected before data reaches any analytics pipeline.
Quality Dimensions
Accuracy
Completeness
Consistency
Validity
Timeliness
Missing Data Imputation
Causes include sensor failure, battery drain, and network loss. A sequence of 20, 22, ?, 25, 26 is interpolated to 23.5. Methods: Mean, Median, KNN, Regression, MICE.
Example: 960 of 1,000 expected readings → 96% completeness.
Bias Detection
A face-recognition model trained on 90% male images performs poorly on female faces. Detection pipeline: Dataset → Bias Metrics → Fairness Check → Balanced Dataset.

Ethical Data Management
Collecting data responsibly is as important as collecting it efficiently. The guiding principle: capture only the minimum data necessary for the intended purpose, and protect it at every stage.
Data Minimisation
Capture only the attributes strictly required. Avoid storing fields that serve no analytical purpose.
Encryption
AES-256 for data at rest; TLS for data in transit. No plaintext sensitive data on wire or disk.
Anonymisation
Remove or pseudonymise personal identifiers before data enters the analytics pipeline.
Access Control
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) combined with Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) limits exposure.
Privacy-Preserving ML
Federated Learning and Differential Privacy allow model training without centralising raw personal data.
Regulatory Compliance
Align with GDPR and India's DPDP Act 2023 — covering consent, purpose limitation, and data subject rights.

The Green Data Acquisition Pipeline
Every technique in this module contributes one layer to a single, end-to-end sustainable pipeline — from physical environment to ethical AI analytics.
Each stage reduces redundancy, energy consumption, or data risk — making the pipeline sustainable by design, not as an afterthought.

Module 2 — Key Takeaways
1
Redundancy is the enemy of sustainability
Up to 95% of raw sensor data carries no new information. Adaptive sampling and event triggering eliminate waste at the source.
2
Energy savings compound across the stack
Duty cycling, wake-up radios, and compression each cut consumption independently — combined, they extend battery life by orders of magnitude.
3
Intelligence belongs at the edge
TinyML and sensor fusion keep heavy computation local, transmitting only decisions — not raw data streams.
4
Data quality and ethics are non-negotiable
Bias, missing values, and poor governance degrade AI reliability. GDPR, DPDP, and privacy-preserving techniques set the baseline for responsible pipelines.
